questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

The new policy has had A. a positive affect on the company's C. bottom line, but it has D. also caused some negative publicity.

options.text: a positive affect on the company's

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the misuse of the word "**affect**" instead of "**effect**."
 
• In this context, we need a noun to follow the adjective "positive." "**Effect**" is a noun meaning a result or consequence, whereas "**affect**" is primarily a verb meaning to influence.
 
• The phrase should be "**a positive effect on**," which correctly identifies the impact the policy had on the company.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part A** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new policy has had a positive **effect** on the company's bottom line, but it has also caused some negative publicity."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The new policy has had" **– This part uses the present perfect tense correctly to describe an action that began in the past and continues to have relevance.
 
• **Option 3: "bottom line, but it has"** – This part is correct; "bottom line" is a standard business term for net income, and the conjunction "but" properly introduces the contrast.
 
• **Option 4: "also caused some negative publicity"** – This part is grammatically sound and correctly completes the second half of the contrast.
 
• **Affect vs. Effect:** A common mnemonic is **RAVEN**: **R**emember **A**ffect **V**erb **E**ffect **N**oun.

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The painting B. is the most unique C. of all the pieces D. in the gallery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the comparative modifier "**most**" with the word "**unique**."
 
• "Unique" is an **absolute adjective**, meaning it describes a state that cannot be intensified or compared. Something is either unique (the only one of its kind) or it is not.
 
• Using "most unique," "very unique," or "more unique" is considered a logical and grammatical error in formal English because you cannot be "more" of the only one.
 
• The correct phrase should simply be "**is unique**" or "**is the most unusual**" if a comparison is intended.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The painting **is unique** of all the pieces in the gallery."* (Or: *"The painting is the most **remarkable**..."*)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The painting" **– This is the subject of the sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 3: "of all the pieces"** – This prepositional phrase is used correctly to define the group being discussed.
 
• **Option 4: "in the gallery"** – This correctly identifies the location and contains no errors.
 
• **Absolute Adjectives:** Other examples include *dead, square, essential,* and *infinite*. You wouldn't typically say something is "very dead" or "more infinite."

Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Sujit said, "Can you pass me the chilli sauce please?"

options.text: Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce please.
Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce please.
Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce.
Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** Sujit said, "Can you pass me the chilli sauce please?"
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The word "please" indicates a request. Therefore, the reporting verb **"said"** is converted to **"requested"**.
 
 
 
• **"Can" becomes "could":**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said/requested"), the modal verb **"can"** must be changed to its past form **"could"** in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun change:**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun **"me"** refers to the speaker (Sujit), so it changes to the third-person **"him"**.
 
 
 
• **Removal of "Please":**
 
 
• In indirect speech, the word **"please"** is omitted because the sense of requesting is already conveyed by the reporting verb "requested."
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** Since the direct speech is a Yes/No question, we use the conjunction **"if"** or **"whether"** to join the reporting clause and the reported speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce please." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it redundantly includes the word "please" at the end.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce please." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "can" is not changed to "could" and it retains "please."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce." 
 
 
• Incorrect because the modal verb "can" remains in the present tense, which does not match the past tense reporting verb.

**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The decision will have been announced before the meeting concludes.

options.text: Someone will announce the decision before the meeting concludes.
They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.
The decision will be announced before the meeting concludes.
The meeting will have announced the decision.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "will have been announced" is in the **Future Perfect Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Future Perfect Passive to Active, the structure changes from "will have been + V3" to "**will have + V3**".
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence does not specify who is announcing the decision, a generic subject like "They" or "Someone" is used in the active voice.
 
• **Object Placement:** The subject of the passive sentence ("The decision") becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• **Conjunctions:** The phrase "before the meeting concludes" remains unchanged as it provides the time context for the action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Someone will announce..." changes the tense to Future Simple, which alters the original meaning of a completed action in the future.
 
• **Option 3:** "The decision will be announced..." is still in the passive voice and changes the tense to Future Simple Passive.
 
• **Option 4:** "The meeting will have announced..." is logically incorrect as it implies the meeting itself is performing the action of announcing.

• The reporting verb **"said"** remains **"said"** in indirect speech because it is not followed by an object (e.g., "said to me").
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed and replaced by the conjunction **"that"** to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Will to Would):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the future tense modal **"will"** must be changed to its past equivalent, **"would"**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** The sentence follows the standard rule for assertive sentences where the tense shifts backward when the reporting verb is in the past.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The cat drank all the milk.

options.text: All the milk was drunk by the cat.
All the milk is drunk by the cat.
All the milk has been drunk by the cat.
All the milk had been drunk by the cat.

questions.solution:

__

• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past to Passive, the structure used is "**was/were + past participle (V3)**".
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object of the active sentence ("all the milk") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The past tense "drank" changes to "was drunk" because "milk" is an uncountable (singular) noun.
 
• **Agent:** The original subject "the cat" is added at the end, preceded by the preposition "by."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"All the milk was drunk by the cat."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Logic: Let the present ages of A and B be 4x and 5x respectively. Five years later, their ages will be (4x + 5) and (5x + 5). The ratio after 5 years is 5:6.

24x + 30 = 25x + 25

25x − 24x = 30 − 25

x = 5

Present age of B = 5 × 5 = 25

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

Total chairs = 18

Chairs before M = 5 − 1 = 4

Chairs after N = 8 − 1 = 7

Chairs between M and N = Total chairs − (Chairs before M + Chairs after N + 2 for M and N themselves)

= 18 − 13

= 5

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

questions.question: O is the incentre of triangle PQR. If angle POR = 140°, find angle PQR.

questions.question: The length and breadth of a rectangle are in the ratio 14:11, respectively, and the perimeter of the rectangle is 150 cm. If the area of the rectangle is equal to the area of the top surface of a solid cylinder, then find the curved surface area of the cylinder given that its radius is 105% of its height.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio (length : breadth) = 14 : 11

Perimeter = 150 cm

Radius = 105% of height

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 2 × (l + b)

Area of rectangle = l × b

Area of circle = π × r²

CSA of cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let l = 14x, b = 11x

⇒ 2 × (14x + 11x) = 150

⇒ 50x = 150

⇒ x = 3

⇒ l = 42, b = 33

⇒ Area = 42 × 33 = 1386

⇒ π × r² = 1386

⇒ (22 ÷ 7) × r² = 1386

⇒ r² = (1386 × 7) ÷ 22 = 441

⇒ r = 21

⇒ r = (105 ÷ 100) × h

⇒ 21 = (105 ÷ 100) × h

⇒ h = 20

⇒ CSA = 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 21 × 20

⇒ CSA = 2640 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 2640 cm².**

questions.question: A and B together can complete a task in 15 days. If A alone can complete the task in 25 days, how long will B take to complete the task alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B = 15 days

A = 25 days

**Formula Used:**

Work = LCM of times

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Total efficiency = Sum of individual efficiencies

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 15 and 25 = 75

⇒ Efficiency of A + B = 75 ÷ 15 = 5

⇒ Efficiency of A = 75 ÷ 25 = 3

⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 - 3 = 2

⇒ Time of B = 75 ÷ 2

⇒ Time of B = 37.5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5.**

questions.question: What does the term 'sulh-i-kul' refer to in the context of Akbar's reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Universal Peace**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'Sulh-i-Kul'** translates to **“Universal Peace”** and was a cornerstone principle of Emperor Akbar's administration during his reign in the Mughal Empire (1556–1605).
 
• It emphasized **religious tolerance**, equal treatment of all religions, and the promotion of harmony among the diverse religious and cultural communities of the empire.
 
• Akbar developed the concept of **'Sulh-i-Kul'** to ensure a secular governance model where no single religion was given special preference over others, fostering an environment of inclusivity.
 
• The policy of **'Sulh-i-Kul'** was reflected in Akbar's administrative reforms, such as the abolition of the **jizya tax** (a tax imposed on non-Muslims) in 1564 and the appointment of individuals from various religious backgrounds to high-ranking positions in his court.
 
• Akbar also established the **Ibadat Khana** (House of Worship) at Fatehpur Sikri, where scholars from different faiths such as Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, Jainism, and Zoroastrianism could engage in theological discussions, embodying the spirit of **'Sulh-i-Kul'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akbar's Administrative Policies:**

 
 
• Akbar's policies were aimed at creating a unified and stable administration. **'Sulh-i-Kul'** was integral to achieving this goal by promoting peaceful coexistence.
 
• The emperor abolished discriminatory practices like the **pilgrimage tax** on Hindus and allowed Hindus to build temples freely.
 
• He appointed Hindus to high offices, such as **Raja Todar Mal**, who became Akbar's finance minister and implemented the efficient **Zabt revenue system**.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance Under Akbar:**
 
 
• Akbar married Rajput princesses, symbolizing his commitment to integrating different communities.
 
• He founded a new syncretic faith called **Din-i-Ilahi**, which combined elements of various religions and reflected his vision of universal peace.
 
• Akbar abolished the practice of forced religious conversion and allowed freedom of worship for all communities.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Mughal Rulers:**
 
 
• Unlike his predecessors like Babur and Humayun, Akbar took a more **inclusive approach** to governance and focused on integrating diverse communities.
 
• His successors, such as Aurangzeb, deviated from this policy, leading to increased religious intolerance and uprisings.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Ibadat Khana:**
 
 
• The **Ibadat Khana** at Fatehpur Sikri was a unique platform where representatives of various faiths debated theological and philosophical ideas.
 
• It showcased Akbar's commitment to understanding and respecting diverse religious perspectives.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Characteristics of 'Sulh-i-Kul':**

 
 
• It was based on the principles of **justice, peace, and harmony**.
 
• It rejected any form of religious discrimination or persecution.
 
• This policy played a crucial role in stabilizing Akbar's vast and diverse empire.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of 'Sulh-i-Kul':**
 
 
• The policy set a precedent for secular governance in India.
 
• It influenced modern Indian constitutional principles, such as **secularism** and **religious freedom**.
 
• 'Sulh-i-Kul' remains a model for fostering peace and inclusivity in multi-religious societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Pressure and temperature play a critical role** in determining the state of a substance (solid, liquid, or gas). Both factors influence the energy and arrangement of particles in a material, affecting phase transitions like melting, boiling, or condensation.

• **Temperature:** When temperature increases, particles gain kinetic energy. For example, a solid melts into a liquid or a liquid evaporates into a gas due to increased molecular motion.

• **Pressure:** Higher pressure can force particles closer together, stabilizing the solid or liquid state. For instance, water remains liquid at higher temperatures under increased pressure, as seen in pressure cookers.

• **Combined Effects:** The interplay of pressure and temperature is represented in phase diagrams, which show how substances transition between states under different conditions. For example, water's triple point occurs at a specific pressure and temperature, where solid, liquid, and gas phases coexist.

• **Statement Validity:** 

• Statement 1: "Pressure alone determines whether a substance is a solid, liquid, or gas." – *Incorrect*. Pressure alone does not determine the state; temperature is equally important.

• Statement 2: "Temperature alone determines the state of a substance." – *Incorrect*. Temperature alone is not sufficient to determine the state as pressure also plays a role.

• Statement 3: "Both pressure and temperature influence the state of a substance." – *Correct*. Both factors are necessary for determining the state of matter.

• Statement 4: "State changes are unaffected by pressure and temperature." – *Incorrect*. State changes are directly influenced by changes in pressure and temperature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Phase Diagram:** A phase diagram maps the states of a substance under different temperatures and pressures. For example:

• The **triple point** is where all three states (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist.

• The **critical point** is where the liquid and gas phases become indistinguishable.

• **Applications:** 

• Pressure cookers utilize high pressure to raise the boiling point of water, cooking food faster.

• Industrial processes like liquefaction of gases depend on precise control of temperature and pressure.

• **Examples of State Changes:** 

• **Melting:** Solid to liquid (e.g., ice to water).

• **Boiling:** Liquid to gas (e.g., water to steam).

• **Sublimation:** Solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase (e.g., dry ice to carbon dioxide gas).

• **Real-world Observations:** 

• At low atmospheric pressure (e.g., on mountains), water boils at a lower temperature.

• High-pressure systems in industrial refrigeration help liquefy gases like ammonia or carbon dioxide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Critical Temperature:** The temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied, regardless of pressure. For example, the critical temperature of water is 374°C.

• **Boyle’s Law:** At constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume. This law demonstrates the influence of pressure on gaseous states.

• **Charles’s Law:** At constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature. This highlights the role of temperature in determining a gas's behavior.

• **Latent Heat:** The heat required for a substance to change state without changing temperature. For example, latent heat of fusion is the energy needed to convert solid to liquid.

• **Examples from Nature:** 

• Water cycle processes like evaporation, condensation, and freezing depend on pressure and temperature.

• Snow formation occurs when water vapor sublimates into ice at specific low pressures and temperatures.

questions.question: The ______ sector of an economy involves groups of activities related with extraction of raw materials directly from nature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Primary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **primary sector** is the first stage of economic activity that deals with the direct extraction of natural resources from the Earth.

• It includes activities such as **agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining, and hunting**, which directly use natural resources.

• The primary sector forms the foundation of an economy by providing raw materials to the **secondary sector** (manufacturing) and the **tertiary sector** (services).

• Countries with a significant portion of their population involved in the primary sector are often considered **developing or agrarian economies**.

• Examples of industries in the primary sector include **coal mining, oil extraction, and farming**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Primary Sector Characteristics:**

• The primary sector is labor-intensive and often depends on natural factors like **climate, soil fertility, and water resources**.

• It contributes significantly to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** in developing nations.

• This sector employs a large portion of the workforce in countries where industrial and service sectors are less developed.

• **Secondary Sector:**

• The secondary sector involves **manufacturing and industrial production**, where raw materials from the primary sector are processed into finished goods.

• Examples include **steel production, automobile manufacturing, and textile production**.

• This sector is more prominent in industrialized economies.

• **Tertiary Sector:**

• The tertiary sector focuses on providing **services** rather than goods.

• It includes industries such as **banking, education, healthcare, entertainment, and retail**.

• The tertiary sector grows as economies become more developed and urbanized.

• **Quaternary and Quinary Sectors:**

• The **quaternary sector** includes knowledge-based activities like **research, development, and information technology**.

• The **quinary sector** refers to high-level decision-making roles such as **government officials, corporate executives, and policy-makers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Historical Context:** The primary sector was the earliest form of economic activity in human civilization, beginning with **hunting and gathering societies**.

• **Global Examples:** Countries like **India, China, and Brazil** have large segments of their workforce employed in the primary sector, particularly in agriculture.

• **Modern Trends:** As economies develop, there is typically a shift from the primary sector to the **secondary and tertiary sectors** due to advancements in technology and industrialization.

• **Challenges:** The primary sector faces challenges like **climate change, resource depletion, and low economic returns** for workers in developing countries.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Kharif crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Kharif crops** are crops that are sown at the beginning of the monsoon season (June) and harvested at the end of the monsoon season (September-October).

• **Rice** is a significant example of Kharif crop and is widely cultivated in regions with high rainfall and warm temperatures, making it suitable for the monsoon season.

• Other examples of Kharif crops include **maize, millets (bajra, jowar), cotton, groundnut, and pulses**.

• The cultivation of rice requires a hot and humid climate, with an average temperature of **21°C to 37°C** and rainfall of about **100-200 cm**, making it ideal for the Kharif season.

• **Rice** is primarily grown in states such as **West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu**, which experience significant monsoon rainfall.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Characteristics of Kharif Crops:**

• Kharif crops depend heavily on the monsoon rains for water supply.

• They are typically grown in areas that receive high rainfall during the monsoon season.

• The sowing season starts with the onset of monsoon in June, and the crops are harvested in September-October.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Wheat:** It is a Rabi crop, cultivated in winter (October to December) and harvested in spring (March to April). It requires a cooler climate and less rainfall compared to Kharif crops.

• **Watermelon:** It is a Zaid crop, grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons (March to June). It requires a dry climate and sufficient irrigation.

• **Mustard:** It is also a Rabi crop that thrives in a cooler climate and is harvested in spring.

• **Importance of Kharif Crops:**

• Kharif crops like rice are staple foods for a large population in India and provide essential nutrients like carbohydrates.

• They contribute significantly to India's agricultural economy and are vital for ensuring food security.

• Major export items such as basmati rice belong to this category, boosting foreign exchange earnings.

• **Regions Favorable for Kharif Crops:**

• Kharif crops are predominantly grown in states like **Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh**.

• The Indo-Gangetic plains and coastal regions are particularly suitable for rice cultivation due to their fertile soil and adequate water supply.

questions.question: What philosophical system did Lord Mahavira develop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Syadvada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Syadvada** is a fundamental philosophical doctrine of Jainism propounded by **Lord Mahavira**, the 24th Tirthankara.

• The term **Syadvada** is derived from the Sanskrit word "Syat," which means "maybe" or "in some respect," emphasizing the concept of relativity and conditionality in truth.

• It is a theory of **sevenfold predication (Sapta-bhangi Nyaya)** that explains how truth can be expressed in seven different ways, depending on perspectives and conditions.

• The doctrine promotes **Anekantavada** (the principle of manifold perspectives), which asserts that reality is complex and multifaceted, and no single viewpoint can capture the whole truth.

• The purpose of Syadvada is to encourage tolerance, non-absolutism, and open-mindedness in understanding the nature of reality and the views of others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Philosophical Systems Mentioned in the Options:**

• **Dualism:** A concept primarily associated with Western philosophy, particularly the ideas of René Descartes, which separates reality into two distinct substances: mind and body. It is unrelated to Jain philosophy.

• **Vedanta:** A Hindu philosophical system based on the Upanishads, focusing on the nature of Brahman (ultimate reality) and Atman (soul). It contrasts with the Jain emphasis on non-absolutism and Syadvada.

• **Mimamsa:** An orthodox Hindu school of philosophy that emphasizes the interpretation of Vedic texts and rituals, unrelated to Jainism or Syadvada.

• **Lord Mahavira and Jain Philosophy:**

• Lord Mahavira, born in **599 BCE** in Kundagrama (modern-day Bihar, India), was the last Tirthankara in Jainism and a key figure in consolidating Jain doctrines.

• He emphasized principles like **Ahimsa** (non-violence), **Satya** (truth), and **Aparigraha** (non-possessiveness).

• Jain philosophy is built on three core principles: **Anekantavada** (pluralism), **Syadvada** (conditional truth), and **Parigraha** (restraint).

• **Sevenfold Predication of Syadvada:**

• **Syat asti:** "In some respect, it exists."

• **Syat nasti:** "In some respect, it does not exist."

• **Syat asti nasti:** "In some respect, it exists and does not exist."

• **Syat avaktavyam:** "In some respect, it is indescribable."

• **Syat asti avaktavyam:** "In some respect, it exists and is indescribable."

• **Syat nasti avaktavyam:** "In some respect, it does not exist and is indescribable."

• **Syat asti nasti avaktavyam:** "In some respect, it exists, does not exist, and is indescribable."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Relevance of Syadvada in Modern Times:**

• Syadvada fosters **intellectual humility** and encourages the acceptance of multiple perspectives, making it relevant in resolving conflicts and promoting dialogue in diverse societies.

• It aligns with the Jain principle of **Ahimsa**, as respecting different viewpoints helps avoid verbal and ideological violence.

• **Comparative Analysis with Other Philosophies:**

• Unlike absolutist philosophies, Syadvada rejects the notion of a single, universal truth, emphasizing conditional and contextual understanding.

• It complements scientific methods that rely on **hypotheses and perspectives** to explain phenomena.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the Indus Valley Civilization city of Rakhigarhi located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rakhigarhi** is one of the largest sites of the **Indus Valley Civilization** (IVC), located in the **Hisar district** of **Haryana, India**.
 
• The site dates back to the **Harappan period (approximately 2600–1900 BCE)** and is considered a critical location for understanding the urban planning, trade, and culture of the IVC.
 
• Excavations at Rakhigarhi have revealed evidence of a well-planned city with features such as **drainage systems, granaries, and multi-room dwellings**.
 
• The site has also yielded several artifacts, including **pottery, beads, tools, and seals**, which indicate a high level of craftsmanship and trade links with other regions.
 
• Rakhigarhi is considered unique because of its size and the presence of different phases of the Harappan civilization, from the **early Harappan to the mature Harappan periods**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization (IVC):**

 
 
• The IVC is one of the world’s earliest urban civilizations, flourishing in the **northwestern regions of South Asia** during the Bronze Age (3300–1300 BCE).
 
• Major IVC sites include **Harappa**, **Mohenjo-Daro** (both in present-day Pakistan), **Dholavira** (Gujarat, India), and **Rakhigarhi** (Haryana, India).
 
• The civilization is noted for its **planned cities, advanced drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures**.
 
• The economy relied heavily on **agriculture, trade, and craftsmanship**.
 
 
 
• **Features of Rakhigarhi:**
 
 
• Spanning over **350 hectares**, Rakhigarhi is larger than Mohenjo-Daro, making it the largest known Harappan site.
 
• Recent DNA studies from skeletons found at Rakhigarhi indicate insights into the genetic makeup of the people of the IVC, providing evidence of continuity with modern South Asian populations.
 
• Artifacts such as **terracotta figurines, jewelry, and ceramics** have been discovered, showcasing the artistic and cultural advancements of the time.
 
• The presence of burial sites with grave goods suggests the belief in an **afterlife and social stratification**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options and Their Relevance:**
 
 
• **Punjab:** While the IVC had sites in present-day Punjab (both India and Pakistan), Rakhigarhi is specifically located in Haryana.
 
• **Gujarat:** The IVC site of **Dholavira**, known for its water management systems, is located in Gujarat.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh:** The IVC site of **Alamgirpur** is located in Uttar Pradesh, but it is much smaller compared to Rakhigarhi.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Rakhigarhi:**
 
 
• It offers insights into the evolution of urban centers and the socio-economic life of the Harappans.
 
• The findings at Rakhigarhi contribute to understanding the transition from the early Harappan phase to the mature phase.
 
• The site has been proposed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site due to its historical and cultural importance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Discoveries:**

 
 
• In 2014, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) initiated large-scale excavations at Rakhigarhi, unearthing significant artifacts and structures.
 
• In 2021, DNA analysis of skeletal remains from Rakhigarhi provided evidence regarding the ancestry of the Harappan people.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government is working to preserve Rakhigarhi and promote it as a site of historical tourism.
 
• Efforts are underway to establish a museum at the site to showcase the artifacts and findings.

questions.question: Where was 'carnelian', a stone used by the Harappans for making beads, mostly found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carnelian**, a semi-precious stone, was extensively used by the **Harappans** for making beads, ornaments, and other decorative items.
 
• It was primarily sourced from the **Ratanpur area in Gujarat**, which was known for its abundant deposits of carnelian stones during the Harappan civilization.
 
• The Harappans had developed sophisticated techniques for bead-making, including cutting, shaping, and polishing carnelian into intricate designs.
 
• Gujarat also had significant trading centers like **Lothal** and **Dholavira**, where carnelian beads were crafted and traded, indicating its importance in Harappan commerce.
 
• The presence of carnelian in various Harappan archaeological sites is evidence of its widespread usage and trade within the civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• The Harappan Civilization, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, flourished between **2600 BCE and 1900 BCE**.
 
• It was known for its urban planning, advanced drainage systems, and trade networks spanning across regions.
 
 
 
• **Bead-Making Industry:**
 
 
• Bead-making was one of the prominent industries in Harappan society, with materials like carnelian, agate, and steatite being used extensively.
 
• Specialized techniques, such as heating and coloring carnelian to enhance its appearance, were employed.
 
 
 
• **Trading Centers in Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Lothal:** Known as a major port and bead-making center, Lothal had a specialized dockyard and workshops for crafting beads and ornaments.
 
• **Dholavira:** Another significant Harappan site in Gujarat, Dholavira showcased advanced urban planning and evidence of trade and craft production.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Carnelian:**
 
 
• Carnelian beads were highly valued and were traded not only within the Harappan civilization but also with Mesopotamia and other neighboring regions.
 
• The durability and vibrant color of carnelian made it a preferred material for jewelry and decorative items.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Sources of Stones:**

 
 
• **Agate:** Found in regions like Maharashtra and Gujarat, used for crafting beads.
 
• **Steatite:** Sourced from Rajasthan, used for seals and ornaments.
 
 
 
• **Trade Networks:**
 
 
• Harappans traded extensively with Mesopotamia, Oman, and other regions, exchanging goods like beads, pottery, and textiles.
 
• Evidence of Harappan carnelian beads has been found in Mesopotamian archaeological sites.
 
 
 
• **Craftsmanship:**
 
 
• Harappan artisans were skilled in precision bead-making, using techniques such as drilling and polishing.
 
• The quality of Harappan beads indicates high levels of expertise in lapidary work.
